inspection_summary: Inspected all 4,778 splitlines()-defined lines of the 78-page normalized source. The mathematical text is coherent despite scattered text-layer formula-layout risk. The source yields 52 material units covering its epistemic program, local/global factorization, carrier and density waves, random-matrix transfer and limitations, extreme gaps and values, prime/zero dual descriptions, log-correlation, and source-specific analyses of five claimed reasons to doubt RH. Front matter, page furniture, transitions, and the bibliography are explicitly partitioned below.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the audit target, evidence types, computational-extrapolation warning, and carrier-wave thesis.

sections_inspected.label: 1 Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the skeptical-argument burden, multiple-perspective method, randomness levels, and paper roadmap.

sections_inspected.label: 2 The zeta-function for absurdly large inputs
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses scale-free snapshots to separate local zero geometry from vertical magnitude.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Background on the zeta-function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the functional-equation, Z-function, RH, zero-counting, unfolding, S(t), value-distribution, and gap-bound apparatus.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Misleading ideas about large values
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Diagnoses finite-height Riemann-Siegel bias and states four mistaken computational notions.

sections_inspected.label: 5 Separating out the local zero spacing
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Factorizes local shape from a slow scale factor, defines and measures carrier waves, and relates low-conductor bias to the highest tone.

sections_inspected.label: 6 A random model for the zeta-function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives structural requirements for self-reciprocal/unitary random polynomials and selects quadratic zero repulsion as the operative model.

sections_inspected.label: 7 RMT and L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Surveys universality, zero statistics, Keating-Snaith value modeling, arithmetic corrections, and analogy failure modes.

sections_inspected.label: 8 Waves in a unitary polynomial
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Exhibits carrier waves, derives a density-wave statistic, relates it to S(t), and studies rigidity and extreme gaps.

sections_inspected.label: 9 Extreme values
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Separates carrier and individual-gap contributions, studies gap influence, reframes Lindelof for self-reciprocal polynomials, and motivates mollifiers.

sections_inspected.label: 10 The primes
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reconciles prime-side and zero-side explanations and presents the adjustable hybrid Euler-Hadamard model.

sections_inspected.label: 11 Randomness not involving the zeros
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops log-correlation, clustered maxima, carrier-wave width heuristics, small-wave cascades, moments of moments, and GMC limits.

sections_inspected.label: 12 Claimed reasons to doubt RH: properties of Z(t)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Applies transfer controls to Lehmer pairs and large-value claims, then analyzes the derivative-based large-gap argument and its possible constructive residue.

sections_inspected.label: 13 Claimed reasons to doubt RH: other properties
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Rejects error-term extrapolation and explains Deuring-Heilbronn failure through linear combinations and loss of Euler products.

sections_inspected.label: 14 Discussion of the Mistaken Notions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Revisits computational filters, counterexample search, precise Gram law, sloshing, and finite-size random-matrix controls.

sections_inspected.label: 15 The chicken or the egg?
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contrasts function-first and zero-first explanatory stances and synthesizes the density-wave viewpoint.

sections_inspected.label: Bibliography
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reference list only; no independent semantic units selected.

accepted_units.title: Auditing reasons rather than assigning belief
accepted_units.why_material: Separates refuting evidence for skepticism from proving RH and makes perspective switching and scale-sensitive randomness the paper's method.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes abstract, burden-of-surprise criterion, themes, and the full section roadmap.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose; no formula reconstruction required.

accepted_units.title: A snapshot fixes shape but hides scale
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that normalized local gaps determine a scale-free graph while Selberg-scale magnitude can differ by orders of magnitude, defeating inference from visible shape to size.
accepted_units.context_note: The full absurd-height setup and snapshot definition are retained so the vertical-scale conclusion is not detached from its probabilistic assumptions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose plus displayed height/variance estimates; figure itself is not required.

accepted_units.title: Functional equation, real Z-function, and sign normalization
accepted_units.why_material: Connects several functional-equation forms to a real graphable function and distinguishes immaterial global sign from the nonzero mean bias of zeta.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definitions and Principle 3.2 with its contrast to zeta moments.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed formulas are text-layer recoverable; figure tick material is incidental.

accepted_units.title: RH symmetry and Turing-style zero certification
accepted_units.why_material: Relates critical-line symmetry, real zeros of Z, sign-change counting, the N(T) error term, and S(t) into a formal interval-verification mechanism while warning that graph extrema alone are not equivalent to RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps both the failed graphical converse and the two-count comparison needed for certification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent but coherent in extracted text; exact constants should be checked against typeset source before reuse.

accepted_units.title: Unfolding zeros and separating typical from extreme size
accepted_units.why_material: Normalizes variable zero density, links large gaps to S(t), contrasts conjectural extremes with Selberg-typical values, and explains why a conspicuous computed peak is atypical.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Principles 3.5 and the independence-based diagnosis leading into carrier waves.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed asymptotics have text-layer fraction layout risk; prose conclusions are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Finite-height Riemann-Siegel bias can mimic asymptotic scale
accepted_units.why_material: Explains how the dominant first term and Gram-point sampling create an order-one bias indistinguishable from the extraordinarily slow asymptotic scale in feasible computations.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Riemann-Siegel setup, Gram-point observation, and Principle 4.2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Riemann-Siegel formulas are recoverable from text but should be typeset-verified for exact symbolic use.

accepted_units.title: Three large-value inferences and Gram's-law intuition
accepted_units.why_material: States four recurring extrapolations to be tested and distinguishes usefulness at moderate height from validity as asymptotic intuition.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes attribution cautions and the stronger claim that the proper Gram law becomes asymptotically rare.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose.

accepted_units.title: Nearby zeros determine shape; distant zeros supply a slow scale
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a polynomial product to isolate local zero geometry from a locally constant contribution of distant zeros, giving the foundational three-factor decomposition for Z(t).
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the motivating rejection of individual local spacing as the leading contribution.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Product display is formula-dependent but the factorization is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Carrier waves govern bulk value distribution
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the slow scale factor and shows why persistence across many zeros, not a pointwise CLT alone, lets one L-function dominate a linear combination through most zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the Bombieri-Hejhal application and Principle 5.2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose with a few extracted asymptotic parameters.

accepted_units.title: Partial-Hadamard measurement of a carrier wave
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs a local approximation by moving equally spaced cosine zeros to observed zeros, isolates the scale factor, and records its window dependence.
accepted_units.context_note: The caveat that scale is not uniquely defined without K and that an overwide fit tends to one is essential.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (5.3) and parameter table have layout risk; prose and figure captions make the construction recoverable.

accepted_units.title: The functional equation supplies the highest tone
accepted_units.why_material: Interprets the Riemann-Siegel expansion as an approximately band-limited signal whose gamma-factor fixes the leading frequency and whose Dirichlet coefficients perturb zero locations, explaining low-conductor Gram bias.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes generalization from zeta to degree-d L-functions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Fourier and approximate-functional-equation displays require typeset checking for exact coefficients.

accepted_units.title: A zeta model must preserve self-reciprocity and unitary zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the involution/real-locus analogy and rejects coefficient-random ensembles because they fail either unitary zeros or the observed kind of spacing randomness.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the underdetermination challenge that a credible skeptical ensemble should predict how and when RH fails.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Self-reciprocal identities are formula-dependent but legible.

accepted_units.title: Repulsion parameter selects the CUE Goldilocks regime
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how beta controls gas-to-crystal behavior and why quadratic repulsion fits observed zero gaps and values better than the too-flexible COE or too-rigid CSE.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the distinction between circular ensemble names and Haar classical groups.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Joint density formula is recoverable; plots are illustrative rather than necessary.

accepted_units.title: Random matrices are generators, not the essential content
accepted_units.why_material: Lists distinct generators of the same CUE zero law and compresses the model to beta-two repulsion rather than a matrix ontology.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Principle 6.5 and its historical terminology warning.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Tridiagonal construction notation has mild extraction risk; the principle is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: From local GUE statistics to value recipes
accepted_units.why_material: Separates three stages of RMT influence: limiting local statistics, finite-conductor compact-group value models, and arithmetic recipes with full main terms.
accepted_units.context_note: Clarifies why random matrices remain useful for visualization after recipes supersede them for precise conjectures.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose.

accepted_units.title: Local statistics forget global ensemble geometry
accepted_units.why_material: Defines local statistics and uses determinantal kernels converging to the sine kernel to explain why GUE and CUE share limiting neighbor behavior.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the boundary between normalized distance statistics and absolute locations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Kernel formulas and rescalings have substantial layout dependency; prose safely supports the universality claim.

accepted_units.title: GUE zero statistics predict gaps but not values
accepted_units.why_material: States the Montgomery-Odlyzko law and consequences for simple, small, and large gaps, then identifies primes, finite-height corrections, and value distribution as missing channels.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps limitations with the predictions to prevent overextension of local-statistics transfer.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Asymptotic gap exponents are formula-dependent and should be typeset-verified.

accepted_units.title: Keating-Snaith matches zero density and value distributions
accepted_units.why_material: Matches zeta near height T to characteristic polynomials of size log(T/2pi), explains finite-height value skew and moment constants, and specifies an ensemble of independent windows for global extremes.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both parts of the law and the distinction between a single matrix and many sampled intervals.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Characteristic-polynomial and moment formulas are text-recoverable with minor layout risk.

accepted_units.title: Arithmetic lower-order corrections damp random-matrix extremes
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why a naive independent prime-times-zero refinement cannot generally reproduce lower terms and records systematic damping relative to unitary matrices.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes dependence between hybrid pieces and the recipe as a more precise alternative.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose.

accepted_units.title: Map real Z to rotated polynomials and zeta half-planes to disks
accepted_units.why_material: Distinguishes modeling a real Z-function from modeling complex zeta and justifies the half-plane-to-disk map using normalization and derivative-zero geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes rotation/reflection invariances that later explain sign and reversal phenomena.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mapping exponent in the final line has layout risk; surrounding prose identifies the intended bridge.

accepted_units.title: Statistical sampling excludes pathological unitary counterexamples
accepted_units.why_material: Classifies leading agreement, arithmetic-factor agreement, and pointwise analogy failure, then shows why rare polynomials violating a Lindelof analogue do not invalidate an ensemble prediction.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps probability-scale reasoning and the recipe caveat with the examples.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Ratio displays are formula-heavy; case structure and conclusions are prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Carrier waves inside one degree-1000 unitary polynomial
accepted_units.why_material: Demonstrates a factor-500 scale change within one fixed polynomial, measures it by local zero matching, and shows that a smaller individual gap can host the global maximum when its carrier is larger.
accepted_units.context_note: Extends the v1 example through its K=10 qualification and lower-order local-spacing comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Figure captions and prose carry the evidence; exact graphical amplitudes depend on the omitted images.

accepted_units.title: Density wave as weighted neighbor discrepancy
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces individual gaps with a multiscale density measure, derives a weighted sum of distant-neighbor discrepancies, and matches it to the logarithmic carrier wave.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes nonuniqueness of the window and the product expansion justifying the statistic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Derivation (8.3)-(8.9) is extraction-fragile; the definition, weighting, and conclusion are recoverable from checked prose.

accepted_units.title: S(t) slope reveals an emergent density wave
accepted_units.why_material: Connects increasing or decreasing averaged S(t) to dense or sparse regions and explains carrier waves as collective behavior suppressed at computable heights by rigidity.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the compatibility caveat with leading-order statistical independence and the reset/anticorrelation explanation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose; figures only illustrate the stated relation.

accepted_units.title: Matching mean spacing does not determine matrix size
accepted_units.why_material: Exposes a hidden scaling choice in Keating-Snaith and uses carrier-wave amplitude to reject a larger rescaled system with the same local mean gap.
accepted_units.context_note: Shows why a concatenation of small systems differs from one larger system.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose with simple scaling notation.

accepted_units.title: Spectral rigidity separates universal from arithmetic regimes
accepted_units.why_material: Uses neighbor-spacing variance and S(t) to show where local universal statistics give way to prime-sensitive long-range constraints that limit density waves.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the resurgent low-zero/prime effect and the finite-height CUE comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Numerical plots are supportive; the number-variance identity and interpretation are text-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Small gaps are universal; large gaps inherit rigidity uncertainty
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the robust one-third smallest-gap exponent from quadratic repulsion, notes consequences for derivative moments, and limits large-gap transfer because zeta is more rigid than CUE beyond the universal regime.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the independent-gap heuristic explicitly labeled and preserves the weaker bound actually used later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Tail and exponent formulas require typeset verification; qualitative distinction is clear.

accepted_units.title: An individual gap is lower order than the carrier wave
accepted_units.why_material: Separates two independent contributions to log magnitude and shows that conjectural maximal gaps contribute only a lower-order square-root-log amount.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Principles 9.1-9.3 and the scale comparison motivating the detailed proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed growth rates have text-layout risk but are explicit enough for planning.

accepted_units.title: A large gap compresses neighbors over a proportional range
accepted_units.why_material: Finds the likely neighboring-zero configuration, gives a charge-splitting scaling argument for proportional influence range, and uses moved zeros plus Stirling to bound the gap's log-value contribution by O(g).
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the empirical setup, conceptual proof, and acknowledged real/imaginary log asymmetry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Product calculation near lines 2663-2683 is extraction-fragile; the argument is reconstructible from prose but exact algebra needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Selberg-typical large and small values require many-gap coordination
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that attributing a positive mass of typical extremes to single very large or very small gaps contradicts both gap tails and total gap mass.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides an independent intuition for carrier waves rather than reusing the large-gap calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: A few extracted square-root expressions have layout risk; contradiction structure is clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: For self-reciprocal polynomials, large values have two distinct zero mechanisms
accepted_units.why_material: Uses Backlund's criterion to reframe Lindelof away from unitary-only models, proves one polynomial implication, and distinguishes radial off-circle zeros from angular gap irregularity.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes failure of the converse and why zeta rigidity suppresses the angular mechanism at Lindelof scale.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Proposition proof is formula-dependent and should be checked against typeset source for exact annulus inequalities.

accepted_units.title: Mollifiers must cancel the slow wave, not merely local zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Recasts zeta locally as a slow random amplitude times a unit-spaced polynomial and explains why normalized linear combinations of derivatives share a viable reciprocal mollifier.
accepted_units.context_note: Connects carrier-wave semantics to concrete improvements of Levinson-type methods.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed local approximation and derivative normalization require typeset checking.

accepted_units.title: Primes and zero density are dual explanations of the same wave
accepted_units.why_material: Rejects a literal causal choice between Euler and Hadamard products, sketches the prime-sum CLT mechanism, and assigns universal local behavior to zeros and long-range behavior to primes.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the warning that pointwise CLT alone does not establish persistence across zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Euler/Hadamard and logarithmic decompositions have formula-layout risk; prose states the intended duality.

accepted_units.title: An adjustable Euler-Hadamard product splits prime and zero scales
accepted_units.why_material: Defines a parameterized product whose cutoff trades nearby zeros against small primes and records leading-order splitting and maximum invariance alongside lower-order limitations.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both evidence for approximate independence and the reason not to extrapolate it to exact lower terms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Definitions of PX and ZX are formula-dependent; exact smoothing conventions need typeset/source-reference verification.

accepted_units.title: Prime phases and matrix traces produce log-correlated fields
accepted_units.why_material: Maps prime sums to trace sums, identifies logarithmic covariance, and imports clustered/cascading maxima intuition that explains carrier-wave persistence and depressed extremes.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps theorem-level Gaussian trace statement distinct from the heuristic zeta covariance manipulation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (11.2) is visibly extraction-damaged in coefficients; use prose and original typeset source before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Log-correlation invalidates independent sampling of local maxima
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts the FHK coefficient and tail with naive independent Gaussian samples, then blocks an invalid inference to global extremes by identifying a nonuniform tail factor and switched limits.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both surprising corrections and the explicit non-implication.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Constants in the FHK expansion are formula-dependent and should be typeset-verified.

accepted_units.title: Carrier-wave width is suggested by clustered effective sample size
accepted_units.why_material: Combines theorem lower bounds, FHK effective sampling, and shifted moments to suggest a log-log span while explaining why fixed moments cannot identify bulk-wave width.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the distinction between rare-value moment sensitivity and bulk persistence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Shifted-moment formulas have layout risk; the effective-sample argument is clear.

accepted_units.title: Small waves suggest valleys within valleys
accepted_units.why_material: Extends the carrier concept symmetrically to small values, compares positive and negative shifted moments, and identifies hierarchical wave generation as a currently inaccessible modeling target.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes concrete candidate observables and their confounds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Ratios-conjecture constants require typeset checking; prose open questions are reliable.

accepted_units.title: Moments of moments and GMC encode log-correlated hierarchy
accepted_units.why_material: Records freezing transitions and the convergence of a shifted random zeta function to a randomized Euler product factored into universal GMC and a smooth nonvanishing perturbation.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps convergence topology and the limitation that the generalized function is not directly visualizable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Functional-analytic notation is legible but exact exponents and spaces should be typeset-verified.

accepted_units.title: Transfer to a system where RH is built in blocks skeptical inference
accepted_units.why_material: Defines two controls: a fact shared by unitary polynomials or arising only from finite verified computation cannot itself count as evidence against RH.
accepted_units.context_note: The author explicitly restricts the conclusion to evidential relevance, not proof of RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose.

accepted_units.title: Lehmer pairs show fragility, not evidence of failure
accepted_units.why_material: Shows arbitrarily close gaps are expected in unitary models where RH is true, broadens 'barely true' through carrier perturbations and the de Bruijn-Newman constant, and separates analytic stability from the sought number-theoretic mechanism.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes why the phenomenon was a reasonable historical concern and why multiple fragility notions do not alter the evidence balance.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose with a few numerical examples.

accepted_units.title: Tightly packed spikes are an axis-choice, not an RH contradiction
accepted_units.why_material: Refutes a visual implausibility argument by separating amplitude, horizontal compression, and the already-known existence of many critical-line oscillations.
accepted_units.context_note: Short self-contained objection and reply.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose.

accepted_units.title: Blanc's interpolation identity targets derivatives near an isolated maximum
accepted_units.why_material: Builds the exact setup in which low odd derivatives make one side large while a zeta-specific high-derivative bound may make the integral side small, avoiding immediate dismissal by unitary analogy.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the numerical check, bound range, and why the additional ingredient is specific to L-functions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The interpolation kernel and table are extraction-fragile; exact use requires scan/typeset verification.

accepted_units.title: Repeated differentiation drives zeros toward cosine spacing
accepted_units.why_material: Explains lower and upper derivative thresholds through zero equalization, derives the functional-equation frequency scale, and constructs self-reciprocal/unitary examples that approach the universal cosine attractor too slowly.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps both generic attraction and the counterexamples needed to delimit Blanc's theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Polar-polynomial derivative calculation is heavily layout-dependent; qualitative mechanism is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: A failed Blanc contradiction may bound gaps rather than refute RH
accepted_units.why_material: Enumerates cancellation escape routes, tests the mechanism on likely unitary configurations, and extracts a parameterized polynomial problem whose solution could improve zeta gap bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the almost-sure random-matrix reconciliation as a conjectural limit, not evidence already established.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Tables and derivative inequalities need typeset verification; the logical alternatives are prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Two moment error terms cannot determine RH
accepted_units.why_material: Reconstructs the k/4 extrapolation from two known cases, exposes it as pattern matching by equally simple alternatives, and distinguishes the genuine k=4 structural transition in main-term methods from unsupported error growth.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Hardy-Littlewood motivation and approximate-functional-equation length bottleneck.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moment exponents and polynomial lengths are formula-dependent but readable.

accepted_units.title: Linear combinations lose Euler products and fail RH systematically
accepted_units.why_material: Uses carrier-wave dominance to explain why most zeros can remain critical while crossings create off-line zeros, then identifies loss of Euler product and zeros in absolute convergence as the structural distinction from L-functions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Deuring-Heilbronn example, theorem-level sigma-greater-than-one behavior, and the final question of what the Euler product protects.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Specific character/function formulas have layout risk; structural argument is clear.

accepted_units.title: Wrong large-value notions can still be productive filters
accepted_units.why_material: Separates asymptotically false causal stories from finite-height algorithms that successfully locate records, while showing why truncated initial terms cannot capture the true extreme scale.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both large-gap growth evidence and Riemann-Siegel filtering examples.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Truncated-sum formula has layout risk; method comparison is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: A search for off-line zeros needs a failure model
accepted_units.why_material: Runs the large-gap story backward, notes distant off-line zeros need not create visible anomalies, and argues that computational search should be conditioned on an explicit failure mechanism.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends with the distinct suggestion to inspect unusually small carrier-wave regions, presented as speculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose.

accepted_units.title: Precise Gram law fails under zero sloshing
accepted_units.why_material: Restores Gram's original indexed interlacing, gives an S(t) necessary condition showing its asymptotic rarity, and reframes long coherent displacements as the same density wave that controls carrier amplitude.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the open problem of directly generating density waves and the proposed next structural level beyond them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose with a simple inequality; no figure dependency.

accepted_units.title: Random-matrix controls make Gram-point effects transient
accepted_units.why_material: Derives sign/reversal conjectures from CUE symmetries, matches zeta data at the prescribed finite matrix size, and uses increasing N plus lower-order damping to explain both similarities and statistically significant differences.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes definitions, tables, asymptotic interpretation, and finite-size caveat.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Tables are readable; one entry at line 4401 appears suspicious in extraction and should not be used numerically without source verification.

accepted_units.title: Function-first skepticism versus zero-first explanation
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts accidental-zero and structural-zero worldviews and summarizes how density waves let the zeros determine both scale and local corrections.
accepted_units.context_note: A philosophical conclusion grounded in the mechanisms developed earlier, not independent evidence for RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose.

v1_context_repairs.reason: The immutable span ends at the initial scale-factor definition; lines 1981-2026 supply the K=10 window, figure interpretation, and decisive qualification that local spacing remains secondary and a smaller gap can dominate under a larger carrier.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One carrier wave, three representations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Weighted zero-density discrepancies, averaged S(t) drift, prime-phase sums, and log-correlation are compatible views of the same slow amplitude phenomenon.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source treats 'arises from' as explanatory language; it does not establish a privileged causal direction or an exact identity among all four models.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Why finite computation reverses the hierarchy of causes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: At computable heights an order-one local-gap or first-term bias can dominate the tiny carrier scale, even though the carrier controls the bulk and extreme asymptotic magnitude.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conclusion is based on the source's stated asymptotic conjectures and model transfer; it is not a direct computation beyond the accessible range.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Universality has a scale boundary
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Quadratic repulsion robustly transfers finite normalized local statistics and the smallest-gap exponent, while long-range rigidity, large gaps, values, and lower terms retain arithmetic information.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The precise crossover scale and maximal-gap constant remain unresolved in the source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A disciplined filter for evidence against RH
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: An observation is not skeptical evidence if it occurs in unitary models where the RH analogue is built in or only inside verified computation; a credible failure claim needs an L-function-specific mechanism and a model for off-line zeros.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Passing this filter would make evidence relevant, not prove RH false; random-matrix transfer itself remains statistical and approximate.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A refutation can leave a fertile gap problem
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Blanc's derivative identity and zeta-specific derivative bound may constrain how a large gap and its compressed neighbors survive repeated differentiation, redirecting an RH contradiction attempt into an upper-gap method.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The polynomial problem is proposed, not solved, and transfer of its techniques back to zeta is speculative.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Gram structure is a finite-conductor shadow of the highest tone
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Early Gram interlacing comes from functional-equation frequency dominance, whereas growing S(t) produces coherent sloshing that destroys indexed interlacing while leaving local one-zero frequencies near their random-matrix limit.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Finite-size tables support the interpretation but do not by themselves prove every claimed convergence rate.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A hierarchy of probabilistic models
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: CUE captures finite-scale zero/value laws, hybrid products reintroduce prime/zero scale tradeoffs, and GMC captures a universal log-correlated limiting factor, with each representation preserving different information.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: None is presented as an exact generative model for lower-order zeta behavior.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Stabilizing the wave through analytic operations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Mollification counteracts slow amplitude variation while repeated differentiation regularizes zero spacing toward a cosine, illustrating two distinct operations that suppress different sources of irregularity.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The mechanisms are analogous only at a conceptual level: the source does not identify mollification with differentiation.
